v.title: FIFA’s 96‑Year World Cup Sell‑Off: A Crisis That Could Hit Barça’s Future
v.excerpt: FIFA’s 96‑year World Cup sell‑off plan could upend Barça’s finances—what this means for the club and its players in 2025.
v.body:
## Quick take
The leaked FIFA documents reveal a 96‑year plan to sell stakes in the World Cup—Infantino’s private‑equity scheme that could reshape global football finance and threaten the commercial stability of clubs like Barça.

## What happened
The documents, now publicly available, outline a multi‑decade strategy for FIFA to divest its World Cup assets, turning the tournament into a long‑term revenue stream for the governing body. Infantino’s plan, described as a “failed private equity model,” would have shifted ownership stakes from national associations to FIFA, creating a 96‑year lease on the event’s profits.

This revelation comes amid growing criticism that the president’s tenure has been marred by opaque deals and governance gaps. The leak suggests that FIFA’s financial future may be tied to a single, highly lucrative asset—an arrangement that could destabilise the balance of power in international football and leave clubs exposed to shifting revenue structures.

## Why it matters
- **Commercial risk for Barça**: The club’s reliance on World Cup‑related income streams, such as broadcast deals and sponsorships, could be jeopardised if FIFA reallocates the tournament’s profits. A 96‑year sell‑off might force clubs to renegotiate long‑term contracts, squeezing budgets that fund star acquisitions and youth development.
- **Impact on player contracts**: High‑profile players like Raphinha or Pedri may find their contracts tied to performance metrics linked to World Cup revenues. A shift in FIFA’s ownership model could alter those metrics, potentially affecting salary caps and transfer valuations.
- **Strategic uncertainty for the season**: The 2024‑25 campaign already faces pressure from financial fair play scrutiny. If FIFA’s revenue model changes, Barça could face new financial constraints that limit squad depth and affect competitiveness in La Liga, the Champions League, and the upcoming Copa del Rey.

## What's next
Watch the next FIFA Congress for any amendments to the World Cup ownership clause. A vote could either stall or accelerate Infantino’s plan, directly influencing the club’s budgeting for the next two seasons. Keep an eye on Barcelona’s financial statements for early signs of revenue reallocation, and be ready for potential renegotiations with sponsors who may seek new terms under a changed FIFA revenue model.

*Source: [Leaked FIFA documents show 96-year plan for stakes in WC selloff](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50585622/leaked-fifa-documents-96-year-world-cup-selloff)*
